description:
I am a teacher passionate about learning, creativity, and inclusive education. We enjoy exploring new ideas and creating engaging educational experiences.

We welcome people who are enthusiastic, creative, collaborative, and eager to learn. We are especially looking for team members with skills in game development, programming, UI/UX design, graphic design, and space science. Most importantly, we value teamwork, curiosity, and a shared passion for exploration!
summary:
GALACTIC NEUROCREW is an interactive 2D educational space mission trainer developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.” Designed for children ages 7–12, it features five lunar mission levels and fifteen interactive challenges.

Players manage life support, oxygen, water, energy, radiation protection, food production, and communication delays. Their decisions affect simulated resources and mission outcomes, teaching engineering trade-offs and the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth.

The game connects to NASA DONKI for solar event records (CME, SEP, and geomagnetic storms); NASA EPIC for Earth observations; NASA's Image and Video Library for lunar and space-plant imagery; and NASA Moon Trek for lunar terrain data. It also includes an optional request for historical Mars weather data from InSight. OSDR is documented as a scientific reference but is not directly queried.

Inclusion is a core design principle. The game features an adaptation for neurodivergent children, with illustrated pictograms integrated into challenges and decision options, visual instructions, and audiovisual navigation. These features support diverse communication, sensory, and learning needs.

By combining NASA data, interactive STEM education, and inclusive design, GALACTIC NEUROCREW makes space exploration more accessible to every child.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS: GALACTIC NEUROCREW

Delia Gaibor Sánchez: Inclusive Educator, Project Creator and Developer

Gerard Guadalupe Gaibor: Creative Ideas and Brainstorming Contributor

How it works?

We developed GALACTIC NEUROCREW as an interactive 2D educational space mission trainer for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.” Our goal was to create an engaging space exploration experience for children ages 7–12, featuring five lunar mission levels and fifteen interactive challenges.

In the game, children take on the role of junior astronauts responsible for managing a lunar outpost. They face different situations involving life support, oxygen, water, energy, radiation protection, food production, and communication delays. Every decision affects the simulated resources and mission outcomes, allowing players to discover the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth through experimentation and problem-solving.

To bring real space science into the experience, Delia incorporated NASA DONKI for solar event records (CME, SEP, and geomagnetic storms), NASA EPIC for Earth observations, NASA's Image and Video Library for lunar and space-plant imagery, and NASA Moon Trek for lunar terrain data. The game also includes an optional request for historical Mars weather data from InSight. OSDR is documented as a scientific reference.

Benefits of use:

One of the main benefits of our project is that it transforms space science into an interactive learning experience. Children can develop critical thinking, decision-making, resource-management, and problem-solving skills while discovering concepts related to space exploration and STEM.

Gerard contributed ideas and suggestions based on his own experience as a neurodivergent child, helping shape the inclusive adaptation for neurodivergent children, including the use of illustrated pictograms in challenges and selectable decision options.

Delia designed a responsive interface that adapts to different screen sizes, allowing children to use the game on mobile phones, tablets, desktop computers, and laptops. The game also includes visual instructions, subtitles, and audiovisual navigation, together with accessibility settings such as adjustable text sizes, high-contrast mode, reduced-motion preferences, and independent sound and music controls.

Intended impact:

With GALACTIC NEUROCREW, we want to make space education more accessible, engaging, and inclusive. Our intention is to encourage children to explore science, technology, engineering, and mathematics through interactive lunar mission scenarios that invite them to think, make decisions, and learn from their choices.

As a neurodivergent child, Gerard believes every child should have the opportunity to discover the universe, develop their abilities, and imagine themselves as part of future space exploration missions. He wants to reduce barriers to learning by considering children with different communication, sensory, and learning needs.

Tools and technologies:

Delia is the teacher and developer. She developed the project as a web application using HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) with a modular architecture for the game mechanics, interactions, and simulation logic. She used JSON for structured data and configuration, Fetch API to retrieve NASA open-data resources, and inline SVG for original 2D illustrations, characters, environments, and decision pictograms.

She also used Vite as the development and production build tool, browser Local Storage to preserve player progress and accessibility preferences, and Progressive Web App (PWA) technologies, including a web app manifest and service worker, to support installation on compatible devices. The application does not require specialized hardware. It runs in a modern web browser and adapts to mobile phones, tablets, laptops, and desktop computers. Delia deployed the project through GitHub Pages, and its source code is publicly available at:

https://github.com/deliainclusiveapps/Galactic-NeuroCrew.git

Creative approach:

What makes GALACTIC NEUROCREW special is the way we combined lunar mission simulation, interactive storytelling, NASA open-data resources, original 2D illustrations, and inclusive communication design in one experience. One of the most important aspects of our creative approach is the integration of pictograms directly into the gameplay. They are not simply decorative icons; they are visual communication elements that help children understand and interact with the available choices.

Factors considered:

Throughout development, we considered the age of the intended audience, educational value, scientific context, usability, accessibility, and compatibility with different devices and screen sizes. Delia paid particular attention to using age-appropriate language, clear visual explanations, progressive challenges, and immediate feedback. Delia also considered the importance of distinguishing real NASA observations from educational simulations, ensuring that the game's simulated resource values are not presented as official NASA measurements or mission limits.

Accessibility was another essential consideration. Delia designed and implemented the accessibility features, including subtitles, narration options, adjustable text, high-contrast mode, and reduced-motion settings, while ensuring a clear and consistent interface across devices. Gerard contributed ideas and suggestions for the illustrated pictograms, helping make the decision options more accessible and understandable for children.

We wanted to create more than a space game, we wanted to build an educational experience where science, technology, creativity, and inclusion come together, making the adventure of space exploration accessible to every child. In this way, inclusion becomes part of the actual gaming experience.
